title: 2009 HMMT November Guts Problem 21
statement:
Let \(f(x)=x^{2}+2 x+1\). Let \(g(x)=f(f(\cdots f(x)))\), where there are \(2009 f \mathrm{~s}\) in the expression for \(g(x)\). Then \(g(x)\) can be written as

\[g(x)=x^{2^{2009}}+a_{2^{2009}-1} x^{2^{2009}-1}+\cdots+a_{1} x+a_{0}\]

where the \(a_{i}\) are constants. Compute \(a_{2^{2009}-1}\).

solutions.text:
\(2^{2009} f(x)=(x+1)^{2}\), so \(f\left(x^{n}+c x^{n-1}+\ldots\right)=\left(x^{n}+c x^{n-1}+\ldots+1\right)^{2}=x^{2 n}+2 c x^{2 n-1}+\ldots\). Applying the preceding formula repeatedly shows us that the coefficient of the term of second highest degree in the polynomial doubles each time, so after 2009 applications of \(f\) it is \(2^{2009}\).
\(2^{\text {nd }}\) ANNUAL HARVARD-MIT NOVEMBER TOURNAMENT, 7 NOVEMBER 2009 - GUTS ROUND
